newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary research group sees 2-2.5 pct growth in 97.
newsitem.headline: Hungary research group sees 2-2.5 pct growth in 97.

text.p: The Hungarian economy should emerge from stagnation next year with gross domestic product likely to grow by between two and 2.5 percent, the private Financial Research Institute said on Monday.

"Usually our forecasts are quite pessimistic but you can say that after the stabilisation (of 1995) we are beginning to see a better trend," Arnold Ludanyi, an industrial economist at the institute, told a news conference.
Hungary's GDP is expected to grow only nominally this year.
The institute said the main factors contributing to higher growth next year would be likely increases of 1.5 percent in household consumption and 7.0 percent in investment spending.
The institute said a side effect would be a worsening of the current account deficit next year, which could hit $2.7 to $2.9 billion, compared to $2.3 to $2.4 billion this year.
The current account deficit narrowed to $2.5 billion last year from $3.9 billion in 1994 and the target this year is about $2 billion.
But Ludanyi said the deficit would not be so significant as to require austerity measures such as those enacted by former finance minister Lajos Bokros. @
Bokros sharply curbed spending on imports by imposing an eight percent import surcharge in 1995. The surcharge is being phased out gradually and will be totally lifted by mid-1997.
The institute said in a statement it had taken the Hungarian economy longer than anticipated to recover from the Bokros measures.
The institute predicted inflation, as measured by the consumer price index, would average 23 to 24 percent this year but would drop to 20 to 21 percent next year.

The institute said it expected the government would have to retain the crawling peg devaluation of the forint, which is now devalued by 1.2 percent every month. The peg might be reduced by 0.1 or 0.2 percentage points but it will not be scrapped, the institute said.
